claims.text: The target materials are high-entropy alloys containing multiple principal elements.
Machine-learning models that account for interactions among multiple principal elements could enable more accurate prediction of high-entropy-alloy melting temperatures.
Such machine-learning models could enable more computationally efficient prediction of high-entropy-alloy melting properties.
Machine-learning models can capture nonlinear relationships between composition and melting properties in high-entropy alloys.
Capturing nonlinear composition–melting-property relationships leads to more accurate predictions.
The proposed models will improve predictive accuracy relative to current traditional methods.
The proposed models will improve computational efficiency relative to current traditional methods.
Validity requires sufficient training and validation data.
Validity requires properly calibrated and validated machine-learning models.
The hypothesis is limited to high-entropy alloys with multiple principal elements and may not apply to other alloy types.
Model performance may depend on the quality and quantity of training data.
Model performance may depend on architecture and hyperparameter choices.
